title: Your EV Has a SECOND Battery. Here's Why 🔋🔌 #shorts

scenes.text: Your electric car has a huge battery. It also has a small one, like a gas car's. Why?
It's a twelve volt battery, and it wakes the car up, running the computers, locks, lights and screens.
Its biggest job: closing the contactors, heavy duty switches that connect the high voltage pack.
When the car is off, or after a crash, they open, cutting the big pack off.
There's no alternator. Instead, a DC to DC converter steps the pack's voltage down to keep it charged.
So if it dies, you may not unlock or drive the car, even with a full main battery.
Some new cars are moving to forty eight volts. Will the twelve volt battery vanish? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
